gen-dafont-true-north-gf-marcellus-sc: Stocky, stubborn, and a little bold: True North packs its lowercase deep into the line and leaves its curves open. And Marcellus SC, a classic serif, brings a literary hush with soft stroke modulation and pulled-back terminals.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-montagu-slab: Squat and blunt, True North holds its curves open while its low-contrast strokes keep everything looking solid and modern. Montagu Slab, a classic serif, reads easily with sturdy downstrokes, slender turns and a generous x-height.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-halant: Visitor looks like old pixel-era hardware, with gaping e shapes, stubby ascenders and strokes pulled like solder through a nozzle. Halant, a serif, offers the opposite, with outward-pointing terminals, a mild thick-thin shift and a towering x-height that steadies longer reading.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-hedvig-letters-ser: Hedvig Letters Serif reads with open-ended curves and a sturdy lowercase, its arches thinning slightly as they leave the stem. Hedvig Letters Serif gives text its weight, while Visitor does its best work as a wire-like, nostalgic heading.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-serif-hentaig: Retro and wiry, Visitor draws every stroke with no thick or thin parts at all. But Noto Serif Hentaigana, a refined text face, adds open jaws on its curves and subtle modulation that never turns dramatic.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-ovo: Ovo, a classic serif, reads gently, its thins only a touch lighter than its thicks and its curve endings spaced wide open. Visitor's heavy bowls and gaping e give headings a nostalgic bite, while Ovo softly carries the text.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-esteban: Woodgod announces itself with a commanding vintage look, its wide channels cut deep into every bowl. Yet Esteban, a classic serif, answers with refined, lightly engraved contrast and an open e that never looks pinched.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-faustina: Faustina, a text serif, draws bowls that thin gracefully and a jaw-open c like a pair of pliers, with a faint swell in each curve. Beside Woodgod's vintage swagger, it settles into a steady, authoritative read.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-halant: Woodgod cuts a wide channel into every bowl, giving its vintage heading a commanding, towering lowercase. But Halant, a serif, does the quieter work, with outward-pointing terminals and the mild variation of a dip pen used gently.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-hedvig-letters-ser: Hedvig Letters Serif reads with open-ended curves, a sturdy lowercase and moderate thick-thin modulation that feels authoritative. And Woodgod works best when its vintage heading gets generous size, leaving the serif body at a more modest one.
